verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents OAuth as an API auth method, and OAuth access tokens carry scopes: creating an event-type webhook requires the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope. The hosted MCP server also uses an OAuth grant flow instead of an API key, so scoped, revocable delegation to an agent is plausible. However, the only scope evidenced is that single one, and plain API keys (managed under settings, test/live prefixes) show no scoping or permission restriction. Missing for 10: a documented scope catalog, per-key permission/least-privilege controls on API keys, agent-specific credential issuance guidance, and independent corroboration.
